summary: The article accurately describes the provisions of Section 80D for senior citizens under the old tax regime, including deduction limits, eligible expenses, and payment modes. It is a reliable source of information.

claims.claim: Senior citizens (60 years and above) can claim a deduction of up to ₹50,000 under Section 80D of the Income Tax Act.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the ₹50,000 deduction limit for senior citizens under Section 80D.

claims.claim: This deduction is available for medical expenses incurred, even if they do not have a health insurance policy.
claims.note: Authoritative sources confirm that senior citizens without health insurance can claim medical expenses under Section 80D.

claims.claim: To avail this benefit, senior citizens must opt for the old tax regime when filing their Income Tax Return (ITR).
claims.note: Deductions under Section 80D are only available under the old tax regime.

claims.claim: The expenses covered include medical treatment, consultation fees, and other related costs for the senior citizen or their dependent parents.
claims.note: Medical expenses generally include consultations, medicines, and treatments. The deduction can be claimed for the senior citizen themselves or their dependent parents.

claims.claim: Payments for these medical expenses must be made through non-cash modes like cheque, demand draft, or digital payment methods, except for preventive health check-ups which can be paid in cash up to ₹5,000 within the overall 80D limit.
claims.note: Non-cash payments are generally required for medical expenses, but preventive health check-ups up to ₹5,000 can be paid in cash within the overall limit.

claims.claim: If you are an individual (not a senior citizen yourself) and your parents are senior citizens, you can claim a separate deduction of up to ₹50,000 for their health insurance premiums or medical expenses, provided you pay for them and they are dependent on you.
claims.note: An individual can claim up to ₹50,000 for health insurance premiums or medical expenses of senior citizen parents, even if the parents are not financially dependent.

article_title: ITR 2026: Senior Citizens Can Claim ₹50,000 Medical Deduction
